# Bram Holmmoor

Bram Holmmoor is a Geospatial Analyst at Nexlet Robotics, a company specializing in automated roof condition scoring to accelerate insurance claims processing. Since joining Nexlet in 2018, Bram has focused on interpreting post-event satellite imagery to assess structural damage, enabling faster, more accurate claims decisions.

Before Nexlet, Bram worked from 2014 to 2018 at SkyTrace Analytics, where he contributed to flood extent modeling and catastrophe response projects. Notably, he played a key role in deploying rapid-response mapping tools during the 2017 Hurricane Orion impact simulation, codenamed Project TempestEye, which improved damage detection turnaround by 30%.

Bram’s specialties include multi-spectral image analysis, change detection algorithms, and integrating satellite data with ground-truth reports. His working style emphasizes close collaboration with data scientists, claims adjusters, and field response teams to refine model outputs and prioritize critical areas for inspection.

At Nexlet, Bram frequently partners with the AI development team and emergency response coordinators, ensuring that satellite insights translate into actionable intelligence during disaster recovery efforts.

Current employer: [[companies/nexlet-robotics]].
